name: Bhote Koshi–Trishuli flood: lower valley close-up
method: Mean of all dates before vs mean of all dates after (averaging removes speckle), HH polarization, 3×3 smoothing, change ≥3 dB, only on valley floors (<40 m above the lowest point within 1.5 km, Copernicus DEM), excluding layover/shadow and anything that also changed between early and late pre-flood dates (control). Patches smaller than 0.02 km² removed. Rougher patches count as flood only within 400 m of the smoother/wetter flooded channel; the rest are labelled seasonal (paddy drainage and harvest).
story_en: NISAR compared 6 radar images before and 5 after the flood of 26 Aug 2026. Along the Trishuli river from Betrawati to Galchhi it shows the flood's path: 1.9 km² of river channel became wider and filled with wet sand and mud (blue), and 0.3 km² next to it became rougher with debris (red). Farther from the river, 4.3 km² of fields also changed, but that is the rice harvest of the monsoon season, so we show it separately and do not count it.
why_not_obvious_en: A flood in a narrow Himalayan gorge does not leave a big lake for a radar to see: the water passes in hours, NISAR returns every 12 days, the river is only a few pixels wide, and steep walls hide parts of the valley. What remains are scars: debris, eroded banks and new channels. That is what this layer shows.

sources.radar: NISAR L2 GCOV, PROVISIONAL (NASA/JPL/ISRO, ASF DAAC), DOI 10.5067/NIL2GCOV-P1

note: 10 m close-up of the lower valley (Betrawati to Galchhi) from the data team's nepal_lower package. Before/after are means of all passes; colours: cyan = smoother/wetter channel (HH down >=3 dB), orange = rougher debris (HH up >=3 dB), grey = layover/shadow, yellow = seasonal (rice harvest, not counted).
